record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: After the complexity gaps in Table 1 are resolved for Pareto-optimal and stable matchings under uncertain preferences, determine the analogous complexity of computing or reasoning about popular matchings when agents' preferences are uncertain.

evidence.quote: After Pareto optimal and stable matchings, one might consider to investigate other fairness notions under uncertain preferences, such as popular or rank-maximal matchings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a bipartite matching market with a set $A$ of applicants and a set $P$ of posts (or, more generally, a two-sided market with men and women). Each agent has a strict preference order over a subset of acceptable agents on the other side. A matching $M$ is a set of acceptable pairs such that every agent appears in at most one pair. Given two matchings $M$ and $M'$, an agent prefers $M$ to $M'$ if either the agent is matched in $M$ and unmatched in $M'$, or the agent is matched in both and prefers its partner in $M$ to its partner in $M'$. We say $M'$ is "more popular than" $M$ if strictly more agents prefer $M'$ to $M$ than prefer $M$ to $M'$. A matching $M$ is popular if no matching is more popular than $M$.

Now suppose preferences are uncertain: each agent $a$ is given a set $\mathcal{L}_a$ of possible strict preference lists (the uncertainty is described, for example, by a lottery, a partial order to be completed, a pairwise uncertainty model, or by joint probability distributions). A preference profile is a choice of one preference list from $\mathcal{L}_a$ for each agent $a$. For each natural model of uncertain preferences (uncertainty/lottery model, joint probability model, compact indifference model, pairwise model, multilayer model, aggregated model, robust model), determine the computational complexity of the following decision/search problems:

(i) Given an instance with uncertain preferences and a matching $M$, decide whether $M$ is popular with positive probability, certainly popular, or maximize the probability that $M$ is popular.
(ii) Decide whether there exists a matching that is popular with positive probability, and decide whether there exists a matching that is popular under every realization (certainly popular).
(iii) Compute a matching maximizing the probability of being popular.

Classify each such problem as polynomial-time solvable or NP-hard (and where relevant, identify the precise complexity class), both in the one-sided (house-allocation) setting and in the two-sided (stable-marriage style) setting.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Bullinger and others, 2023–2024) has substantially addressed this question. For popular matchings under uncertain/multilayer/aggregated/robust preference models, all four models lead to NP-hard problems in the two-sided setting (existence of certainly popular matching is NP-hard even with one side fixed), while one-sided instances admit polynomial-time algorithms. For dominant matchings, the robust and uncertainty models are polynomial while multilayer and aggregated models remain NP-hard. Thus the problem is largely resolved for the standard uncertainty models, though finer-grained complexity questions and other uncertainty models may remain.

status_evidence.title: Popular and Dominant Matchings with Uncertain, Multilayer and Aggregated Preferences
status_evidence.snippet: Four models (Uncertainty, Multilayer, Robust, Aggregation) are analyzed; for two-sided preferences all four lead to NP-hard problems for popular matchings, while one-sided cases are polynomial-time solvable.
status_evidence.claim: Complexity of popular matchings under uncertain preferences is largely characterized across standard models.

status_evidence.title: Robust Popular Matchings (AAMAS 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies robust popular matching problem under preference uncertainty and establishes complexity results.
status_evidence.claim: Robust popular matching complexity has been analyzed.
